title.narrative: Green and inclusive valorization of cotton and textile for local empowerment

description.narrative: In Mali, the textile sector is primarily based on cotton cultivation, the country’s second-largest export commodity after gold. In 2023, the cotton industry accounted for approximately 7% of total exports and contributed nearly 15% of the national GDP. It plays a vital role in the country’s economic and social development by generating income for over 4 million people—representing about one-fifth of the population—and promoting economic inclusion in both rural and urban areas.This project is aligned with a national ambition to sustainably and inclusively develop this strategic yet underutilized sector. Currently, less than 5%[1] of Mali’s cotton is processed locally, with the vast majority exported in its raw form. This limited value addition restricts the sector’s ability to create decent jobs, particularly for youth and women, who remain largely excluded from formal value chains.The project therefore seeks to accelerate impact by strengthening climate-resilient local solutions, expanding economic opportunities for youth and women, and reinforcing the resilience of cotton-dependent communities facing compounded socio-economic, environmental and security pressures. In this context of escalating climate shocks, declining cotton productivity, and heightened youth vulnerability in fragile regions, there is an urgent need to consolidate and scale up gains achieved under previous JSB/TICAD-supported interventions such as the completion of the diagnostic study on the cotton sector and cotton linter developpement by local enterprises, the national textile research center and integration of digital tools in textile artisans work. Building on those earlier investments that laid the foundations for inclusive value chain development and local processing, this project is designed as a time-sensitive continuation and scale-up, responding to emerging risks while safeguarding livelihoods and employment opportunities.
